## Context / Problem

The legacy `reconcile` family spans CLI registration, direct-engine modes, library/MCP `mode=` acceptance, compatibility profiles, exit behavior, manifests/tallies, and `bridge_state/reconcile-check.json`. It is not a simple rename. In particular, historical `"reconcile-check"` state appears in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:658,717`.

## Approach

This container separates canonical bridge capability migration from deletion of legacy command/mode/state surfaces. Child 1 maps and implements all useful reconcile-check observables under `bridge preview`, `bridge fsck`, `bridge status`, or one coherent new bridge diagnostic subverb. Child 2 removes CLI/direct-engine modes and persisted-state compatibility only after migration. Child 3 removes library/MCP compatibility methods and schemas after the new bridge contracts are live.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Canonical bridge operations retain or explicitly retire every current reconcile-check observable with documented evidence.
- [x] No live route, mode, state path, docs, schema, or compatibility profile retains
      `reconcile` or `reconcile-check` vocabulary -- **except one operator-directed carve-out,
      now tracked separately.** The reconciler pause writer and its decoder at
      `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:717` and `:658` still persist
      `gated_mode="reconcile-check"`; the "Final AC2 Option B execution note" below records
      that this pass was explicitly directed not to edit them. Filed as
      `extralegal-durative-beaver` (d433-782d-e74d-4b27), linked `discovered_from` this
      ticket, with ACs requiring the writer and decoder to move together so existing pause
      records stay readable. Whole-tree sweep at `12a10f3ab4ef` confirms the rest is clean
      (`.github/`, `Jenkinsfile`, `scripts/`, `src/rebar/schemas/` all free of it); the only
      other survivors are intentional -- the narrow decode alias AC3 retains (`mode.py:57`),
      the retirement rejection message that must name the term to route users
      (`request.py:102-104`), ADR prose, the unrelated review-bot log key
      `reconcile_check_error` (`review_bot/reconcile.py:350`), and frozen eval fixtures.
- [x] Persisted historical reconcile-check data is migrated or read by a narrowly retained decoder until safe to retire.
- [x] CLI, Python, and MCP consumers use explicit bridge operations rather than compatibility `mode=` dispatch.

## Final AC2 Option B execution note

The human operator selected Option B for this final in-scope completion pass: retire the residual live `reconcile-check` vocabulary from the reconciler mode taxonomy, bridge-runner compatibility profile, GitHub Actions/Jenkins provider mode choices, live schema prose, live operator docs, and affected tests while preserving the read-only discrepancy capability through `bridge preview` / `dry-run` routing.

AC3 carve-out and decoder refinement: the operator explicitly directed this pass not to edit `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` at the pause-state decoder/writer lines around 658/717. Because that carved-out writer still persists the historical pause sentinel `gated_mode="reconcile-check"`, this pass keeps a narrow `Mode.from_str()` decode alias that maps only that persisted sentinel to the live cap-0 `DRY_RUN` floor. The alias is not a selectable enum member, is not listed in `MODE_CAPS` or allowed-mode errors, and exists only so AC3 historical pause data keeps blocking write-capable modes (`bootstrap-strict`, `bootstrap-throttle`, `live`) while live route/profile/mode/docs/schema vocabulary is retired.
